1Q1.label: Table masked (one table removed)
1Q1.mask_target: One entire table hidden from masked DDL
1Q1.llm_can_succeed_when: Source NL describes only visible tables; Text2Schema recovers visible structure. Hidden table recovery requires guessing from dangling FK references (rare).

1Q2.label: Attributes masked (PK/FK structure only)
1Q2.mask_target: Non-key column definitions removed; PK/FK column names remain
1Q2.llm_can_succeed_when: LLM recovers key columns from NL (often copied from constraint lines). Non-key attributes must be hallucinated or omitted.

1Q3.label: Domain integrity masked (types, NULL/NOT NULL)
1Q3.llm_can_succeed_when: Structure is fully visible in masked DDL; LLM can recover tables/columns/FKs well. Types/nullability are partially inferable from NL semantics (dates, amounts, names).

1Q4.label: Entity integrity masked (PRIMARY KEY, UNIQUE)
1Q4.llm_can_succeed_when: Columns and FKs visible; PK often inferable from `_id` naming and FK targets. Composite PKs and UNIQUE constraints are harder.

1Q5.label: Referential integrity masked (FOREIGN KEY, REFERENCES)
1Q5.llm_can_succeed_when: Full table/column/PK structure visible; FKs inferable from `_id` / `table_id` naming and NL relationship descriptions.

1Q6.label: All table names anonymized (table_1, table_2, …)
1Q6.mask_target: Semantic table names replaced with placeholders
1Q6.llm_can_succeed_when: Source NL often maps table_N to semantic names (cities, countries). Text2Schema can recover meaningful names if NL disambiguates placeholders.

precision_issues: Attribute precision exceeds recall: Text2Schema tends to invent columns/tables not in gold (especially when source NL is verbose or hallucinates during schema→text).
FK precision > FK recall: model adds plausible but incorrect foreign keys (_id naming heuristics, over-connected schemas).
PK/UNIQUE precision > recall: extra primary keys declared on obvious id columns even when gold uses composite or alternate keys.
pk_hallucination flagged in 72 records: declaring PKs on columns that are not gold PKs.
table_hallucination in 49 records: extra tables invented (junction tables, lookup tables).
recall_issues: Low overall table recall (31.4%): many gold tables omitted, especially Case 1Q1 (hidden table) and large schemas.
Low attribute recall (13.8%): majority of gold columns missing in reconstructed schema; worst for Case 1Q2 (non-key columns not in masked input).
FK recall 5.5%: referential structure largely lost unless explicitly stated in NL (Case 1Q5) or inferable from naming.
fk_miss failure mode in 1155 records: fewer than half of gold FKs recovered.

codellama.summary: Attr F1=0.178, FK F1=0.075, Table F1=0.438. Precision generally exceeds recall on attributes (0.321 vs 0.123).

mistral.summary: Attr F1=0.212, FK F1=0.091, Table F1=0.468. Precision generally exceeds recall on attributes (0.349 vs 0.153).

inferability_insights.interpretation: Hidden tables rarely recovered (hidden table recall via aggregates). Non-inferable attr recall 0.0%.
Inferable (PK/FK) attr recall 6.8% vs non-inferable 8.7%. LLM succeeds on key columns visible in masked DDL; fails on hidden attributes.

qualitative_patterns.llm_comparison: Mistral-sourced NL yields higher attribute recall (0.153 vs 0.123) and FK recall (0.060 vs 0.049). CodeLlama NL tends to produce sparser schemas (fewer recreated tables: 4781 vs 4616).
qualitative_patterns.nl_leakage: Source NL leaks non-inferable info in some cases: {'mentions_hidden_table': 82, 'mentions_hidden_column': 849, 'uses_anonymized_table_names': 253}. When NL mentions hidden tables/columns, Text2Schema may appear to 'recover' non-inferable elements — partly propagation of schema→text hallucination.
